description: Install Ollama into your home directory (no root) and run it as a user process bound to 127.0.0.1:11434, then pull the chosen model. Nothing is installed system-wide and no sudo is used. The Open WebUI plugin reuses this same Ollama and its models automatically.

steps.description: Download the standalone Ollama binary into ~/.local (no root, no systemd; recent builds ship as .tar.zst and need the 'zstd' unpack tool). Skipped if Ollama is already installed.
steps.run: set -e; mkdir -p "$HOME/.local"; case "$(uname -m)" in x86_64|amd64) A=amd64 ;; aarch64|arm64) A=arm64 ;; *) echo "Unsupported architecture: $(uname -m)" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac; command -v zstd >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Ollama ships as a .tar.zst archive and needs the 'zstd' tool to unpack. Install zstd (e.g. apt-get install zstd / dnf install zstd) and retry." >&2; exit 1; }; echo "Downloading Ollama ($A) into ~/.local ..."; TMP=$(mktemp); curl -fsSL "https://ollama.com/download/ollama-linux-$A.tar.zst" -o "$TMP"; zstd -dc "$TMP" | tar -xf - -C "$HOME/.local"; rm -f "$TMP"; "$HOME/.local/bin/ollama" --version || { echo "Ollama installed but failed to run — your server's glibc may be too old (needs GLIBC 2.28+, e.g. Ubuntu 20.04+ / RHEL 8+)." >&2; exit 1; }

steps.description: Start the Ollama server as a user process (binds to 127.0.0.1:11434) and wait until it answers.
steps.run: export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"; export OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11434; mkdir -p "$HOME/.local"; nohup ollama serve >"$HOME/.local/ollama.log" 2>&1 & for i in $(seq 1 30); do curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0; sleep 1; done; echo 'Ollama did not become ready; last log lines:' >&2; tail -n 20 "$HOME/.local/ollama.log" >&2 2>/dev/null || true; exit 1

steps.description: Download the chosen model (skipped if already present).

uninstall.description: Remove the Ollama binary, libraries and downloaded models from your home directory (can be several GB).
